items.title: RPKI now protects 70% of internet routes
items.summary: 📝 Now that enough networks check, they are dropping these invalid routes. Gray: share of a country's routed IPv4 prefixes that are RPKI-invalid. Blue: share of its IPv4 addresses in invalid routes, weighted by how many vantage points see each route.🔗 Read more: https://ipinfo.io/blog/rpki-protects-70-internet-routes

items.title: Business accounts will consent to Meta scraping their websites Starting Oct. 30
items.summary: 📝 The updated terms explicitly state that Meta can use the content it collects from associated websites to “train” Meta products. Meta declined to answer a list of questions about these updated terms. The update also states that Meta can create “test credentials” in order to scrape websites associated with business accounts.🔗 Read more: https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/10/metas-new-commercial-terms-will-allow-the-scraping-of-news-sites-legal-experts-say/

items.title: Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad
items.summary: 📝 Sill Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad. Sill shows a window from your Mac, or the whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad. Nearby, your device finds your Mac with Bonjour on your local network.🔗 Read more: https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill

items.title: BeBox is a Haiku application that emulates Be Inc.'s BeBox
items.summary: 📝 It runs both PowerPC models from their original boot ROMs, with BeOS for PowerPC from Developer Release 6 through R5. It also runs the Hobbit prototypes that came before them, built around two AT&T Hobbit processors, with Be's 1993-94 system from their surviving disks. The newer boot ROMs stop at their boot menu when no boot volume is set yet: press Return.🔗 Read more: https://github.com/johnrash/bebox

items.title: Comparing Chromium Development at Google and Igalia
items.summary: 📝 Google is owned by institutional investors, while Igalia is owned by employees, which the audience applauded. Chrome is a Google product, with Google branding and colors, while Chromium is an open-source project that anyone can use to build a browser. Obviously, the proprietary pieces are handled elsewhere, but she and other Google Chrome developers rarely have to interact with that code.🔗 Read more: https://lwn.net/Articles/1094721/
